description: Power Usage Effectiveness assumed for hyperscale data centres. Retained for traceability; not validated for target-year forecasting.
source: EPRI 2026; average U.S. data centre PUE estimated at 1.32 in 2024, with large hyperscale facilities potentially as low as 1.1. Shehabi et al. 2024 supports low hyperscale PUE assumptions.
denominator: annual facility energy / annual IT energy
population: Legacy Nordic modelling assumption; cited foreign evidence is not a Nordic calibration

description: Facility-level annual load factor for hyperscale data centres, defined as average realised grid-side load divided by reported or estimated grid-side/nameplate capacity. Retained for traceability; not validated for target-year forecasting.
source: EPRI 2026; observed large hyperscale facility annual load factor of 75% relative to nameplate capacity. Shehabi et al. 2024 used only as supporting evidence on high relative hyperscale server operational time.
denominator: annual average facility electrical load / compatible available facility nameplate MW
population: Legacy Nordic modelling assumption; cited foreign evidence is not a Nordic calibration

description: Power Usage Effectiveness assumed for hyperscale AI data centres. Retained for traceability; not validated for target-year forecasting.
source: EPRI 2026; large hyperscale facilities with liquid cooling may reach PUE as low as 1.1. Shehabi et al. 2024 models AI data centres separately by cooling system.
denominator: annual facility energy / annual IT energy
population: Legacy Nordic modelling assumption; cited foreign evidence is not a Nordic calibration

description: Facility-level annual load factor for hyperscale data centres with substantial AI workloads. Treated as high-utilisation but not full nameplate operation. Retained for traceability; not validated for target-year forecasting.
source: EPRI 2026; hyperscale observed annual load factor of 75% relative to nameplate capacity. Shehabi et al. 2024 distinguishes AI training and inference operational time. Regen/National Grid DSO 2025 notes AI training is relatively flat while inference is peakier.
denominator: annual average facility electrical load / compatible available facility nameplate MW
population: Legacy Nordic modelling assumption; cited foreign evidence is not a Nordic calibration

description: Power Usage Effectiveness assumed for AI/HPC-oriented facilities. Retained for traceability; not validated for target-year forecasting.
source: Shehabi et al. 2024; AI data centres modelled separately for air and liquid cooling. EPRI 2026 supports lower PUE for newer large facilities.
denominator: annual facility energy / annual IT energy
population: Legacy Nordic modelling assumption; cited foreign evidence is not a Nordic calibration

description: Legacy 0.80 value retained only for traceability. Server operational time does not establish facility load factor. Not eligible as an empirical default.
source: Shehabi et al. 2024; AI training server operational time assumed at 80%, varied between 75-85%. EPRI 2026 provides facility-level support that hyperscale load factors can be high but below nameplate.
denominator: annual average facility electrical load / compatible available facility nameplate MW
population: Legacy Nordic modelling assumption; cited foreign evidence is not a Nordic calibration

description: Power Usage Effectiveness assumed for colocation facilities with AI workloads. Retained for traceability; not validated for target-year forecasting.
source: EPRI 2026; average U.S. data centre PUE estimated at 1.32 in 2024, with older/smaller facilities higher. Shehabi et al. 2024 supports colocation PUE below roughly 1.4 in recent years.
denominator: annual facility energy / annual IT energy
population: Legacy Nordic modelling assumption; cited foreign evidence is not a Nordic calibration

description: Facility-level annual load factor for colocation facilities with AI-oriented workloads. Set above conventional colocation due to AI/HPC tenants, but below dedicated hyperscale or AI/HPC facilities. Retained for traceability; not validated for target-year forecasting.
source: EPRI 2026; smaller multi-tenant co-location facilities averaged 57% annual load factor relative to nameplate. Regen/National Grid DSO 2025 notes colocation load is relatively consistent due to tenant diversity, while AI workloads may increase variability.
denominator: annual average facility electrical load / compatible available facility nameplate MW
population: Legacy Nordic modelling assumption; cited foreign evidence is not a Nordic calibration

source: EPRI 2026; average U.S. data centre PUE estimated at 1.32 in 2024, with older/smaller facilities higher. Shehabi et al. 2024 supports colocation PUE below roughly 1.4 in recent years.
denominator: annual facility energy / annual IT energy
population: Legacy Nordic modelling assumption; cited foreign evidence is not a Nordic calibration

description: Analyst-selected PUE sensitivity bracket; endpoints are scenarios, not observed Nordic bounds. No central value.
source: EPRI Powering Intelligence 2026 gives efficiency context across facility types; selection of the bracket is an analyst assumption.
source_locator: Section Annual and Peak Electricity Use; paragraph on capacity-weighted PUE
denominator: Annual facility energy / annual IT energy; applied to capacity only as a labelled model approximation
population: Illustrative Nordic application of foreign technology context; not a fitted population estimate

description: Two reference utilisation cases. Not a confidence interval, Nordic calibration or AI workload prediction. Applies to available operational nameplate, not grid connection or realised peak.
source: EPRI Powering Intelligence 2026 reports 0.57 for smaller multi-tenant facilities and 0.75 for one large single-tenant facility; transfer to this portfolio is illustrative.
source_locator: Figure 3 and paragraph beginning Finally, we must estimate annual and hourly utilization
denominator: Average facility electrical load / available operational facility nameplate; deployment separately represents incremental capacity available during the year
